notes: Confirmed via BenQ's official Asia-Pacific spec page (fetched twice, consistent results) and corroborated by independent search snippets listing the same port counts. Port breakdown per BenQ specs: HDMI 3x in / 1x out (all HDMI 2.0); VGA 1x in; USB-A 3x USB2.0 + 2x USB3.0; USB-B (touch) 3x USB2.0; USB-C 1x USB3.0 (front, supports video/audio/touch/charging); Audio: 2x 3.5mm line-in (1 mic, 1 PC audio), 1x 3.5mm line-out, 1x S/PDIF optical out; RJ45 10/100/1000 (1000 via internal OPS slot, 10/100 for onboard Android SoC — modeled as a single eth-1g port since it is one physical jack); RS-232 1x. One HDMI input and 2 USB-A (2.0) ports are front-mounted per BenQ marketing copy ("two built-in USB 2.0 ports and an HDMI port in front"); the remaining ports are rear-mounted. Exact front/rear split for the 2x USB3.0 ports could not be confirmed and is assumed rear. The unit also has an internal OPS slot (slot-in PC bay) — this is a proprietary card-slot, not a standard external connector, so it was omitted from the port list. AC power inlet connector type (IEC C13/C14) was not explicitly published by BenQ in the sources checked; it is inferred from the standard practice for BenQ interactive flat panels in this power class (121.5W typical, 100-240V 50/60Hz) — flagged as an inference, hence "medium" confidence overall. No rack-mount units apply; this is a 75" wall/stand-mounted interactive flat panel, not rack-mountable.
